sources.entry: Deep Learning Book by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville

summary.name: Deep Learning (Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville)
summary.one_liner: A free online textbook by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville that introduces machine learning and deep learning, published in print by MIT Press.
use_cases: looking up math notation used in ML papers
course reading material for deep learning
finding a LaTeX template and notation page for writing
summary.what_it_does: The page is the online edition of the Deep Learning textbook, intended to help students and practitioners enter machine learning and deep learning. Its table of contents covers applied math and ML basics (linear algebra, probability and information theory, numerical computation, machine learning basics), modern practical deep networks (feedforward networks, regularization, optimization, convolutional networks, sequence modeling, practical methodology, applications), and deep learning research. The site also offers downloadable LaTeX style and notation template files. The authors accept typo reports and exercise suggestions by email, but they state that the book is complete and now makes only small corrections.
notable: Online version is complete and free to read, published in print by MIT Press (also orderable on Amazon)
Downloadable LaTeX style, math notation, and notation page templates
Covers math prerequisites through deep networks, sequence models, and research topics
Chinese translation rights bought by Posts and Telecom Press
caveats: No PDF download; the web version is HTML, which the authors say is a form of weak DRM required by the MIT Press contract
Printing works best from Chrome; some known rendering issue in outdated Edge versions
